{"results": {"web": [{"url": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Switch_2", "title": "Nintendo Switch 2", "description": "", "page_age": "2026-09-24T02:58:12", "thumbnail_url": "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/c9/Nintendo_Switch_2_logo.svg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=original", "favicon_url": "https://you.com/favicon?domain=en.wikipedia.org&size=128", "contents": {"highlights": ["# Nintendo Switch 2
- **Connectivity**: Wi-Fi 6 Bluetooth Headphone jack 2 × USB-C Dock: 2 × USB 2.0 1 × Gigabit Ethernet 1 × HDMI 2.1
- **Power**: 3.78 V 19.74 Wh 5,220 mAh Li-ion battery Duration: 2–6.5 hours
- **Current firmware**: 23.0.0 (September 10, 2026 (2026-09-10)) \[±\]", "Nintendo revealed the Switch 2 on January 16, 2025, and announced its full specifications and release details on April 2. Pre-orders in most regions began on April 5. The system received praise for its social and technical improvements over its predecessor, though the increased prices of both the console and its games library were criticized. More than 3.5 million units were sold worldwide within four days of release, making the Switch 2 the fastest-selling Nintendo console.", "## History
### Development
Rather than the rail system used on the original Switch, the new Joy-Con are connected using magnetic connections. Nintendo had originally explored magnetic connections for the first Switch model but the connection was determined to be too wobbly. With the Joy-Con 2, they refined the magnetic approach, making the connection stronger and easily removed with a mechanical release system. With this new system, the Joy-Con now audibly snap when the magnetic connection is made, which Dohta said helped to symbolize the Switch branding.", "The Pro Controller was also similarly redesigned for the Switch 2, smoothing out the motions of the joysticks, and adding an audio jack and two programmable buttons in the grips that the player can customize.", "### Industry rumors
Industry rumors began as early as 2019 of a high-end model of the Switch, often nicknamed the "Nintendo Switch Pro" in the media; many of the speculated features became part of the OLED Switch model, released in 2021. Nintendo confirmed it was working on its next gaming system during a call with investors in October 2020.", "While Nintendo officially acknowledged the development of the Switch's successor by May 2024, rumors and leaked photos of a new console persisted through 2024, as well as a data breach from Game Freak on the development of the next *Pokémon* game for the Switch's successor.", "### Announcement and promotion
#### Pre-orders
Retailers began receiving shipments in late May 2025. Some who had pre-ordered Switch 2 consoles posted footage two weeks prior to the release, though they were unusable without a day-one patch.", "## Hardware
### Console
Along with the existing layouts from the Nintendo Switch's design, which includes a USB-C port on the bottom that serves as its power source and connector within a dock, a headphone jack, and a cartridge slot, the Nintendo Switch 2 adds an internal microphone with noise cancellation and a second USB-C port on the top of the unit for charging the console when on tabletop mode, and for use with accessories like external cameras. The console also has a redesigned stand with adjustable angle, similar to that used on the Switch OLED model.", "The original Switch included an OLED revision, and while Nintendo had considered using OLED for the Switch 2, hardware design lead Tetsuya Sasaki said they opted to use LCD due to the advancements in LCD technology including support for HDR. Unlike the first-generation model, the dock also contains a built-in Ethernet connector and a cooling fan. The cooling fan is only intended to cool the dock itself, not the Switch 2 console.", "In January 2025, alleged images of the system's motherboard appeared. Richard Leadbetter of *Digital Foundry* concluded that, rather than porting the Ampere-based architecture to a smaller process node, it is more likely that the existing low-cost Samsung 8 nm process node is being used. While such a process poses difficulties for performance and battery life, Leadbetter believed these can be relieved due to the nature of fixed hardware platforms, which allow for custom software optimizations to be implemented.", "In June 2025, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang claimed the processor's semiconductor process technology employs optimizations for "ultra low power".", "#### Hardware protections
Numerous outlets have reported that the Switch 2's dock communicates using a non-standard proprietary protocol rendering existing third-party docks incompatible, as those intended for the original Switch or USB-C DisplayPort Alt mode are unable to communicate with the console. This incompatibility was attributed to the Switch 2 console requiring a 20 volt power supply to enter docked mode. In the months following release, third-party docks compatible with the Switch 2 became available.", "A system software patch for the Switch 2 released in November 2025 appeared to eliminate the video output signal from the console to some third-party docks, rendering them unusable. Nintendo asserted that with the patch, the company "does not have any intention to hinder or invalidate legal third-party dock compatibility".", "In May 2025, Nintendo announced an update to the North American Nintendo Account user agreement and privacy policy which, if broken by users of the Switch 2, could "render the Nintendo Account Services and/or [*sic*] the applicable Nintendo device permanently unusable in whole or in part". This was expected to be in an attempt to stop piracy and emulation of games. The agreement also pertains to installing unauthorized software or modifying the hardware to make it run faster.", "### Joy-Con 2
See also: Joy-Con § Joy-Con 2

The Joy-Con 2 controllers

The Joy-Con 2 controllers have an updated design from the original Joy-Con. Besides being larger to match the console, they attach magnetically by snapping to the sides rather than using a rail system. They are removed using a small button on the Joy-Con 2 that causes a cylinder inside to extend and push off from the main unit. Nintendo stated that their analog sticks would be larger, smoother, and more durable.", "Early reports suggested the new controller thumbsticks would use Hall-effect sensors to address the drift issues that the original models had due to dust collecting within the analog system but Nintendo stated in April 2025 that Hall-effect sensors are not used.", "The SL and SR buttons on the side of the controllers have been significantly enlarged, and a new C button is present on the right Joy-Con 2 to activate the new GameChat feature. The controllers are also able to be used like a computer mouse in supported games by sliding them across a surface. Both Joy-Con 2 controllers have a 500mAh battery that is estimated to last 20 hours. The controllers can be recharged by connecting them to the console or by using the Charging Grip.", "The infrared sensor from the first-generation Joy-Con has been removed.", "### Revisions
According to a report from Nikkei, Nintendo is developing a revision of the Switch 2 which includes user-replaceable batteries for the console and the Joy-Con 2. This is to comply with the European Union's right to repair regulations, which require easy replacement for rechargeable batteries. The revision is only planned to be released in Europe.", "Nintendo confirmed that it would start shipping these models across Europe in July 2026, with all regions receiving these by early 2027; at the same time the company announced it was discontinuing the original Switch family in Europe by February 2027.", "## Software
### Distribution
Nintendo said that the introduction of game-key cards was to help future-proof the Switch 2 for many years, as that games keep growing larger and surpass the storage limit of game cards, using game-key cards still allows such games to be sold through retail in addition to digital distribution. Games that come on a Game-Key Card are not locked to a Nintendo account.", "### Online services
Nintendo also released a new iteration of the GameCube controller alongside the platform's addition to Nintendo Classics, available exclusively to existing Switch Online subscribers. Switch 2 exclusive games cannot be purchased using earlier Game Vouchers that had been available on the original Switch.", "A voice chat service known as GameChat allows users to conduct voice chats and screen sharing with friends. GameChat supports video calls using an optional webcam accessory. It is accessible via a "C" button on the right Joy-Con 2, on the new GameCube controller, and on the Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller. Chat was free to use until March 31, 2026, after which point a paid Nintendo Switch Online membership is required to use the feature.", "The console's reveal trailer in January 2025 was accompanied by early footage of *Mario Kart World*, later announced to launch alongside the Switch 2 on June 5. First-party Switch games for 2025 such as *Metroid Prime 4: Beyond* and *Pokémon Legends: Z-A* released with "Nintendo Switch 2 Edition" versions at launch, with graphical and performance enhancements. The *Nintendo Switch 2 Welcome Tour* game was revealed in the April 2 Direct, releasing as an online exclusive alongside the console launch.", "### Third-party support
In May 2024, Nintendo announced their intentions to acquire Miami-based developer Shiver Entertainment from its prior parent company Embracer Group, with the company detailing in a statement that the merger enabled them to procure specialized in-house resources for the development and porting of software, while allowing the studio to continue commitments to Switch and other platforms.", "*Bloomberg News* later reported that the acquisition was for bolstering Nintendo's efforts in securing games from third-party developers on Switch 2, with Shiver assisting external developers in the optimization of such games from competing platforms. In September 2024, developer Pathea Games announced *My Time at Evershine*, the spiritual successor to *My Time at Portia* (2019) and *My Time at Sandrock* (2023).", "Both EA and Take-Two Interactive also formally committed to bringing their respective sports franchises, *EA Sports FC*, *Madden NFL*, *WWE 2K*, and *NBA 2K* to the platform. Nintendo was also revealed to be collaborating with partner studios on exclusive games for the system, such as *Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment* with Koei Tecmo, *Kirby Air Riders* with Bandai Namco Studios, and *The Duskbloods* with FromSoftware.", "Nintendo later stated in their November 2025 financial results briefing that the Switch 2 had the largest first-year software lineup from third-party developers of any Nintendo system.", "Publisher Ubisoft commented that they were "in love" with the console following its reveal, and released ports of *Star Wars Outlaws* and *Assassin's Creed Shadows* for the system during its launch window. Weicong Wu, producer of *Marvel Rivals*, expressed interest in bringing the game to the Switch 2, having stated that the team has already contacted Nintendo and possessed dev kits. However, he has stated that it will only come to the Switch 2 if the game's performance is satisfactory.", "Around August 2025, Digital Foundry reported that smaller and indie studios had said that Nintendo was not providing Switch 2 hardware development kits, and directing them to focus on releases for the original Switch, which would still be playable on the Switch 2 with backwards compatibility. Nintendo had not made clear what the reasonings behind this was, but this decision was preventing these developers from releasing native Switch 2 games with support for the console's updated hardware or additional functionality like GameChat.", "### Backward compatibility
Hardware director Takuhiro Dohta described the solution as "somewhere in between a software emulator and hardware compatibility" and Tetsuya Sasaki said that the method used is "performed on a real-time basis as the data is read". This method allows Switch games to have Switch 2 features added, such as GameChat support, when played on the Switch 2.", "As of May 2025, of the 122 Nintendo-developed games tested, all were found to be compatible except the Nintendo Labo VR Kit, due to the Switch 2's larger size being unable to fit inside the accessory. As of 27 May 2025, Nintendo had tested 75% of the more than 15,000 third-party Switch games, finding that "around 170" of them had issues while all the rest were compatible.", "In March 2026, a Switch 2 system update introduced the Handheld Boost Mode function: this function, available in the system settings, forces Nintendo Switch software to play in their TV Mode state whilst played on Nintendo Switch 2 in Handheld and Tabletop Modes. Whilst enabling players with generally improved resolution and performance for most original Switch titles, battery life is affected and handheld-specific functions such as the touchscreen are disabled.", "To aid users in bringing their Switch games to the Switch 2, Nintendo introduced Virtual Game Cards for the original Switch system software in April 2025. Virtual Game Cards can be used to virtually transfer digitally purchased games for use on a second Switch or Switch 2 system, or loaned to a family member's Switch for up to two weeks at a time.", "## Reception
### Critical response
*Digital Trends* and *TheGamer* praised the dock's accessible design, while *PCMag* was ambivalent about it; other critics were satisfied by its improved ventilation system. The kickstand was praised for its design improvements and durability by some, though *Wired* was concerned about its security and thinness. The screen, especially given the lack of OLED, was the subject of commentary: *Wired* felt the 120 Hz refresh rate and HDR10 support made up for this.", "The console's social features were praised. *Wired* described GameChat as "the most notable, wholly new feature" of the console, and *Mashable* described Nintendo not as reinventing the wheel with a two-decade-old concept, but moving it "beyond pure utility and into the realm of actively being enjoyable to use". *Business Insider* felt it was "made for quick, casual multiplayer sessions" rather than specialist communication. Critics praised the accuracy of the speech-to-text option and its ability to discern specific speakers.", "Critics praised the built-in microphone's noise cancellation capabilities. Many called GameChat's screenshare choppy. *Mashable* described the Virtual Game Card system as potentially a "logistical nightmare for competitive siblings" squabbling over possession of shared digital games. *IGN* stated that the Switch 2 "doesn't provide many of its own novel reasons to upgrade", scrutinised that Nintendo is "charging a substantial premium" and criticised the lack of comfortability of the Switch 2's Joy-Con and their lack of analog triggers.", "Similarly *Nintendo Life* stated that accessing games comes at a "significant cost" and highlighted the system's 256GB storage among the cons of the console in their review, saying it will "fill up fast". *PC Gamer (US)* said not to buy the Switch 2 if you want cheap games, that the console has a "hefty price tag" and highlighted that the Switch 2 Joy-Con are still capable of getting stick drift."]}}, {"url": "https://www.cnet.com/tech/gaming/nintendo-switch-exploit-fixable-with-update/", "title": "Original Nintendo Switch Owners Should Apply the Latest Firmware Update Now - CNET", "description": "The problem does not affect the Nintendo Switch 2.", "page_age": "2026-09-28T14:29:14", "thumbnail_url": "https://www.cnet.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/a8c10a4d-7339-454b-a123-ff4f36bdcbbd.jpg", "favicon_url": "https://you.com/favicon?domain=www.cnet.com&size=128", "contents": {"highlights": ["# Original Nintendo Switch Owners Should Apply the Latest Firmware Update Now

### News
The News interface was originally available in the 1.0.0 version of the software; however, new headlines were not transmitted until the 2.0.0 update was released. The 3.0.0 update revamped the News system, adding multiple news "channels" for different games that users can subscribe to.  The 4.0.0 update further improved the News screen, updating its layout.", "The 9.0.0 update added search support to the News channel, allowing users to narrow the list via filters or free text. The 10.0.0 update added a "Bookmark" feature, allowing users to save their favorite News articles.", "### Nintendo eShop
Though initially launched as a WebKit-based browser application applet, a major backend redesign switched the storefront into a native application, bringing it in line with the Nintendo Switch Online application. The update was published in June 2026 and sported major performance improvements, dark theme support (if configured from the system settings), the ability to set a passcode to prevent unauthorized purchases and new video player shortcuts.", "### Album
The 2.0.0 update added the ability to post screenshots to Facebook or Twitter from within the system UI, making it easier to share screenshots. The 4.0.0 update added support for saving 30-second videos, in compatible games. The 14.0.0 update added the ability to download screenshots and videos to a PC via a USB cable or to a Mobile device via a webpage hosting the files generated by the Switch.", "### GameShare
While the feature was introduced to the Nintendo Switch in the 20.0.0 update, GameShare requires a Nintendo Switch 2 system in order to share a copy of the game. The feature also works online on the Nintendo Switch 2 via the GameChat service.", "## History of updates
The 20.0.0 update, released on April 30, 2025, added GameShare and Virtual Game Cards, as well as updated icon colours to match the Switch 2's user interface. Only Nintendo Switch 2 systems can initiate GameShare sessions, while all Nintendo Switch console generations may join them. Gaming", "# Witcher 3 Remastered Hits Switch 2 Sept. 29 \[2026\]
Updated Sep 28, 2026 · 13 min read

CD PROJEKT RED’s remastered edition of *The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt* arrives on Nintendo Switch 2 tomorrow, September 29, 2026, closing an 11-year gap since Geralt of Rivia first stepped onto PC and PlayStation 4 in May 2015.", "The release lands as part of a wider wave of AAA remasters and ports reaching Nintendo’s new hardware this year, and it arrives free for anyone who already owns the original game on the platforms CD PROJEKT RED has confirmed. This piece looks at what is actually confirmed for launch day, how the Switch 2 version fits into the console’s growing third-party library, and what the release signals about the remaster economy heading into 2027.", "## What CD Projekt Red confirmed for September 29
The headline fact is simple: *The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered* ships on PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2 on September 29, 2026. CD PROJEKT RED’s announcement describes upgrades to visuals, gameplay, performance, and other unspecified features, without publishing a granular patch-note style breakdown ahead of launch.", "Existing owners on GOG, Steam, Epic Games Store, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S get the remastered version as a free upgrade, no repurchase required. Switch owners of the original 2019 port also get a free claim path to the Switch 2 version once it releases.", "That free-upgrade model is a deliberate contrast to how some publishers have handled remasters this generation, charging $10 to $40 for what amounts to a visual refresh. Our earlier coverage on CDPR’s decision to skip the upsell entirely goes deeper into the business logic behind that call.", "The remastered base game folds in both expansions, *Hearts of Stone* and *Blood and Wine*, at no additional cost for existing owners. That bundling matters for the Switch 2 conversation specifically, because it means the portable version isn’t a stripped-down base-game-only release the way some past Switch ports trimmed content to hit performance targets.", "## Why the Switch 2 version is the story, not the remaster itself
PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S owners already have a version of *The Witcher 3* that runs at or near 60 frames per second with ray tracing options. For them, the remaster is an incremental visual and technical bump on hardware that was already capable.", "Switch 2 is the platform where the question actually matters: can Nintendo’s new hardware, which sits well below PS5 and Xbox Series X in raw compute, run an open-world RPG of this scale without the compromises that defined the original Switch 1 port back in 2019?", "Switch 2’s silicon jump changes the baseline math entirely, and CD PROJEKT RED building the remaster natively for the new hardware, rather than porting the 2019 Switch 1 build forward, is the more relevant technical story for anyone deciding whether to play on the go.", "No official resolution, frame rate, graphics-mode, or download-size numbers for the Switch 2 build had been published as of this writing. Any specific technical claim circulating ahead of launch should be treated as unconfirmed until CD PROJEKT RED or a hands-on outlet publishes tested figures once the update goes live.", "## The Switch 2 port wave: Witcher 3 is not an outlier
*The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered* is landing in the middle of a genuinely crowded season for ambitious third-party ports chasing Switch 2’s new hardware ceiling.", "*Diablo 4: Age of Hatred Collection* reached Switch 2 earlier this month, bundling two expansions into a $69.99 package, evidence that Nintendo’s new console can now carry live-service, loot-heavy ARPGs that would have been unthinkable on the original hardware.", "At the more demanding end of that spectrum sits Rayman Legends Retold, whose PC requirements reportedly call for an RTX 4080-class GPU for 4K/60 performance while still being confirmed for a Switch 2 release.", "That gap between PC recommended specs and a portable console target is exactly why hands-on impressions of games like the *Witcher 3* remaster matter so much this year: publishers are making increasingly bold bets that Switch 2’s architecture and its DLSS-style upscaling tools can close a hardware gap that would have been unbridgeable on Switch 1.", "| Game | Switch 2 status | Notable detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered | Releases Sept. 29, 2026 | Free upgrade for existing owners; includes both expansions |
| Diablo 4: Age of Hatred Collection | Released Sept. 2026 | $69.99, bundles two expansions |
| Metal Gear Solid 4 Remaster | Released 2026 | Confirmed 60fps by Digital Foundry testing |
| Rayman Legends Retold | Confirmed for Switch 2 | PC specs reportedly target RTX 4080 for 4K/60 |
| Control Resonant | PC specs published | RTX 4070 Ti recommended for 60 FPS on PC |", "## CD Projekt Red’s business calculus
A free, high-quality remaster functions as sustained marketing for that upcoming title. Every Switch 2 owner who claims the free Witcher 3 upgrade, plays through 100-plus hours of Geralt’s story, and comes away impressed is a warmer prospective buyer for Witcher 4 than one reached through a traditional ad campaign.", "There’s a hardware-sales angle here too, one that benefits Nintendo more directly than CD PROJEKT RED. A widely known, well-reviewed RPG landing free for anyone who already owns it gives existing Switch and Switch 1 owners on the fence about upgrading a concrete reason to buy Switch 2 hardware now rather than waiting.", "## Historical context: from 2015 launch to 2026 remaster
That earlier update was framed as a free upgrade for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S owners with targeted improvements; this year’s remaster spans four platforms simultaneously, including a from-the-ground-up Switch 2 build, and is being marketed with the “Remastered” label rather than as a next-gen patch.", "It’s the first time CD PROJEKT RED has treated a Switch release of the game as a day-one platform alongside PC and the PlayStation/Xbox family rather than a delayed follow-up port, which is itself a signal of how much confidence the studio has in Switch 2’s hardware ceiling compared to its predecessor.", "## Market impact: what a free AAA remaster does to a launch window
Switch 2 launched into a console market still working through a hardware supply crunch tied to broader memory chip shortages that have pushed up component costs across the industry this year. Against that backdrop, a free, marquee-name RPG landing on the platform functions as a low-cost way for Nintendo to add perceived value to hardware that’s already selling at a premium relative to its predecessor.", "Open-world RPGs releasing in 2026 and 2027 are being built against a much higher visual and systemic bar, and keeping *The Witcher 3* in active rotation, especially on a growing platform like Switch 2, extends the commercial life of a decade-old title without requiring the studio to divert resources away from Witcher 4 development.", "| Milestone | Date | Platform(s) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original launch | May 2015 | PC, PS4, Xbox One |
| Switch port | October 2019 | Nintendo Switch |
| Next-gen update | December 2022 | PS5, Xbox Series X\|S, PC |
| Remastered edition | September 29, 2026 | PC, PS5, Xbox Series X\|S, Switch 2 |", "## What’s still unconfirmed heading into launch
It’s worth being precise about what CD PROJEKT RED has and hasn’t said publicly. The company has not published a standalone retail price for the Switch 2 version for buyers who don’t already own the base game on a qualifying platform. It has not released target resolution, frame rate, or graphics-mode details for the Switch 2 build, docked or handheld. No download size has been disclosed.", "Expect the most reliable data points, docked and handheld resolution figures, sustained frame rate under load, and loading times, to surface within the first 24 to 48 hours after the September 29 release, largely from technical-analysis outlets running side-by-side comparisons against the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S versions.", "## Predictions: what happens after launch day
- Expect the first wave of technical breakdowns within 48 hours of the September 29 release, likely including a Digital Foundry-style frame rate and resolution analysis comparing docked and handheld Switch 2 modes against PS5 and Xbox Series X\|S.", "- The free-upgrade model will likely become the reference point other publishers get measured against the next time a studio tries to charge for a remaster of a game that’s over five years old.
- Switch 2’s third-party library credibility will keep building through Q4 2026 as more mid-generation remasters and ports target the platform, following the pattern set by Diablo 4, MGS4, and now Witcher 3.", "- CD PROJEKT RED will likely use Witcher 3 Remastered’s Switch 2 reception, positive or negative, as a data point in its own public messaging about Witcher 4’s scope and platform ambitions.
- If performance reviews land well, expect a modest bump in Switch 2 hardware attach-rate commentary from Nintendo in its next quarterly investor update, framed around third-party AAA availability rather than first-party software alone.", "## How to claim the free upgrade

highlights:
# Nintendo Switch 2
- **Connectivity**: Wi-Fi 6 Bluetooth Headphone jack 2 × USB-C Dock: 2 × USB 2.0 1 × Gigabit Ethernet 1 × HDMI 2.1
- **Power**: 3.78 V 19.74 Wh 5,220 mAh Li-ion battery Duration: 2–6.5 hours
- **Current firmware**: 23.0.0 (September 10, 2026 (2026-09-10)) \[±\]

Nintendo revealed the Switch 2 on January 16, 2025, and announced its full specifications and release details on April 2. Pre-orders in most regions began on April 5. The system received praise for its social and technical improvements over its predecessor, though the increased prices of both the console and its games library were criticized. More than 3.5 million units were sold worldwide within four days of release, making the Switch 2 the fastest-selling Nintendo console.

## History
### Development
Rather than the rail system used on the original Switch, the new Joy-Con are connected using magnetic connections. Nintendo had originally explored magnetic connections for the first Switch model but the connection was determined to be too wobbly. With the Joy-Con 2, they refined the magnetic approach, making the connection stronger and easily removed with a mechanical release system. With this new system, the Joy-Con now audibly snap when the magnetic connection is made, which Dohta said helped to symbolize the Switch branding.

The Pro Controller was also similarly redesigned for the Switch 2, smoothing out the motions of the joysticks, and adding an audio jack and two programmable buttons in the grips that the player can customize.

### Industry rumors
Industry rumors began as early as 2019 of a high-end model of the Switch, often nicknamed the "Nintendo Switch Pro" in the media; many of the speculated features became part of the OLED Switch model, released in 2021. Nintendo confirmed it was working on its next gaming system during a call with investors in October 2020.

While Nintendo officially acknowledged the development of the Switch's successor by May 2024, rumors and leaked photos of a new console persisted through 2024, as well as a data breach from Game Freak on the development of the next *Pokémon* game for the Switch's successor.

### Announcement and promotion
#### Pre-orders
Retailers began receiving shipments in late May 2025. Some who had pre-ordered Switch 2 consoles posted footage two weeks prior to the release, though they were unusable without a day-one patch.

## Hardware
### Console
Along with the existing layouts from the Nintendo Switch's design, which includes a USB-C port on the bottom that serves as its power source and connector within a dock, a headphone jack, and a cartridge slot, the Nintendo Switch 2 adds an internal microphone with noise cancellation and a second USB-C port on the top of the unit for charging the console when on tabletop mode, and for use with accessories like external cameras. The console also has a redesigned stand with adjustable angle, similar to that used on the Switch OLED model.

The original Switch included an OLED revision, and while Nintendo had considered using OLED for the Switch 2, hardware design lead Tetsuya Sasaki said they opted to use LCD due to the advancements in LCD technology including support for HDR. Unlike the first-generation model, the dock also contains a built-in Ethernet connector and a cooling fan. The cooling fan is only intended to cool the dock itself, not the Switch 2 console.

In January 2025, alleged images of the system's motherboard appeared. Richard Leadbetter of *Digital Foundry* concluded that, rather than porting the Ampere-based architecture to a smaller process node, it is more likely that the existing low-cost Samsung 8 nm process node is being used. While such a process poses difficulties for performance and battery life, Leadbetter believed these can be relieved due to the nature of fixed hardware platforms, which allow for custom software optimizations to be implemented.
In June 2025, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang claimed the processor's semiconductor process technology employs optimizations for "ultra low power".

#### Hardware protections
Numerous outlets have reported that the Switch 2's dock communicates using a non-standard proprietary protocol rendering existing third-party docks incompatible, as those intended for the original Switch or USB-C DisplayPort Alt mode are unable to communicate with the console. This incompatibility was attributed to the Switch 2 console requiring a 20 volt power supply to enter docked mode. In the months following release, third-party docks compatible with the Switch 2 became available.

A system software patch for the Switch 2 released in November 2025 appeared to eliminate the video output signal from the console to some third-party docks, rendering them unusable. Nintendo asserted that with the patch, the company "does not have any intention to hinder or invalidate legal third-party dock compatibility".

In May 2025, Nintendo announced an update to the North American Nintendo Account user agreement and privacy policy which, if broken by users of the Switch 2, could "render the Nintendo Account Services and/or [*sic*] the applicable Nintendo device permanently unusable in whole or in part". This was expected to be in an attempt to stop piracy and emulation of games. The agreement also pertains to installing unauthorized software or modifying the hardware to make it run faster.

### Joy-Con 2
See also: Joy-Con § Joy-Con 2

The Joy-Con 2 controllers

The Joy-Con 2 controllers have an updated design from the original Joy-Con. Besides being larger to match the console, they attach magnetically by snapping to the sides rather than using a rail system. They are removed using a small button on the Joy-Con 2 that causes a cylinder inside to extend and push off from the main unit. Nintendo stated that their analog sticks would be larger, smoother, and more durable.

Early reports suggested the new controller thumbsticks would use Hall-effect sensors to address the drift issues that the original models had due to dust collecting within the analog system but Nintendo stated in April 2025 that Hall-effect sensors are not used.

The SL and SR buttons on the side of the controllers have been significantly enlarged, and a new C button is present on the right Joy-Con 2 to activate the new GameChat feature. The controllers are also able to be used like a computer mouse in supported games by sliding them across a surface. Both Joy-Con 2 controllers have a 500mAh battery that is estimated to last 20 hours. The controllers can be recharged by connecting them to the console or by using the Charging Grip.
The infrared sensor from the first-generation Joy-Con has been removed.

### Revisions
According to a report from Nikkei, Nintendo is developing a revision of the Switch 2 which includes user-replaceable batteries for the console and the Joy-Con 2. This is to comply with the European Union's right to repair regulations, which require easy replacement for rechargeable batteries. The revision is only planned to be released in Europe.

Nintendo confirmed that it would start shipping these models across Europe in July 2026, with all regions receiving these by early 2027; at the same time the company announced it was discontinuing the original Switch family in Europe by February 2027.

## Software
### Distribution
Nintendo said that the introduction of game-key cards was to help future-proof the Switch 2 for many years, as that games keep growing larger and surpass the storage limit of game cards, using game-key cards still allows such games to be sold through retail in addition to digital distribution. Games that come on a Game-Key Card are not locked to a Nintendo account.

### Online services
Nintendo also released a new iteration of the GameCube controller alongside the platform's addition to Nintendo Classics, available exclusively to existing Switch Online subscribers. Switch 2 exclusive games cannot be purchased using earlier Game Vouchers that had been available on the original Switch.

A voice chat service known as GameChat allows users to conduct voice chats and screen sharing with friends. GameChat supports video calls using an optional webcam accessory. It is accessible via a "C" button on the right Joy-Con 2, on the new GameCube controller, and on the Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller. Chat was free to use until March 31, 2026, after which point a paid Nintendo Switch Online membership is required to use the feature.

The console's reveal trailer in January 2025 was accompanied by early footage of *Mario Kart World*, later announced to launch alongside the Switch 2 on June 5. First-party Switch games for 2025 such as *Metroid Prime 4: Beyond* and *Pokémon Legends: Z-A* released with "Nintendo Switch 2 Edition" versions at launch, with graphical and performance enhancements. The *Nintendo Switch 2 Welcome Tour* game was revealed in the April 2 Direct, releasing as an online exclusive alongside the console launch.

### Third-party support
In May 2024, Nintendo announced their intentions to acquire Miami-based developer Shiver Entertainment from its prior parent company Embracer Group, with the company detailing in a statement that the merger enabled them to procure specialized in-house resources for the development and porting of software, while allowing the studio to continue commitments to Switch and other platforms.

*Bloomberg News* later reported that the acquisition was for bolstering Nintendo's efforts in securing games from third-party developers on Switch 2, with Shiver assisting external developers in the optimization of such games from competing platforms. In September 2024, developer Pathea Games announced *My Time at Evershine*, the spiritual successor to *My Time at Portia* (2019) and *My Time at Sandrock* (2023).

Both EA and Take-Two Interactive also formally committed to bringing their respective sports franchises, *EA Sports FC*, *Madden NFL*, *WWE 2K*, and *NBA 2K* to the platform. Nintendo was also revealed to be collaborating with partner studios on exclusive games for the system, such as *Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment* with Koei Tecmo, *Kirby Air Riders* with Bandai Namco Studios, and *The Duskbloods* with FromSoftware.
Nintendo later stated in their November 2025 financial results briefing that the Switch 2 had the largest first-year software lineup from third-party developers of any Nintendo system.

Publisher Ubisoft commented that they were "in love" with the console following its reveal, and released ports of *Star Wars Outlaws* and *Assassin's Creed Shadows* for the system during its launch window. Weicong Wu, producer of *Marvel Rivals*, expressed interest in bringing the game to the Switch 2, having stated that the team has already contacted Nintendo and possessed dev kits. However, he has stated that it will only come to the Switch 2 if the game's performance is satisfactory.

Around August 2025, Digital Foundry reported that smaller and indie studios had said that Nintendo was not providing Switch 2 hardware development kits, and directing them to focus on releases for the original Switch, which would still be playable on the Switch 2 with backwards compatibility. Nintendo had not made clear what the reasonings behind this was, but this decision was preventing these developers from releasing native Switch 2 games with support for the console's updated hardware or additional functionality like GameChat.

### Backward compatibility
Hardware director Takuhiro Dohta described the solution as "somewhere in between a software emulator and hardware compatibility" and Tetsuya Sasaki said that the method used is "performed on a real-time basis as the data is read". This method allows Switch games to have Switch 2 features added, such as GameChat support, when played on the Switch 2.

As of May 2025, of the 122 Nintendo-developed games tested, all were found to be compatible except the Nintendo Labo VR Kit, due to the Switch 2's larger size being unable to fit inside the accessory. As of 27 May 2025, Nintendo had tested 75% of the more than 15,000 third-party Switch games, finding that "around 170" of them had issues while all the rest were compatible.

In March 2026, a Switch 2 system update introduced the Handheld Boost Mode function: this function, available in the system settings, forces Nintendo Switch software to play in their TV Mode state whilst played on Nintendo Switch 2 in Handheld and Tabletop Modes. Whilst enabling players with generally improved resolution and performance for most original Switch titles, battery life is affected and handheld-specific functions such as the touchscreen are disabled.

To aid users in bringing their Switch games to the Switch 2, Nintendo introduced Virtual Game Cards for the original Switch system software in April 2025. Virtual Game Cards can be used to virtually transfer digitally purchased games for use on a second Switch or Switch 2 system, or loaned to a family member's Switch for up to two weeks at a time.

## Reception
### Critical response
*Digital Trends* and *TheGamer* praised the dock's accessible design, while *PCMag* was ambivalent about it; other critics were satisfied by its improved ventilation system. The kickstand was praised for its design improvements and durability by some, though *Wired* was concerned about its security and thinness. The screen, especially given the lack of OLED, was the subject of commentary: *Wired* felt the 120 Hz refresh rate and HDR10 support made up for this.

The console's social features were praised. *Wired* described GameChat as "the most notable, wholly new feature" of the console, and *Mashable* described Nintendo not as reinventing the wheel with a two-decade-old concept, but moving it "beyond pure utility and into the realm of actively being enjoyable to use". *Business Insider* felt it was "made for quick, casual multiplayer sessions" rather than specialist communication. Critics praised the accuracy of the speech-to-text option and its ability to discern specific speakers.

Critics praised the built-in microphone's noise cancellation capabilities. Many called GameChat's screenshare choppy. *Mashable* described the Virtual Game Card system as potentially a "logistical nightmare for competitive siblings" squabbling over possession of shared digital games. *IGN* stated that the Switch 2 "doesn't provide many of its own novel reasons to upgrade", scrutinised that Nintendo is "charging a substantial premium" and criticised the lack of comfortability of the Switch 2's Joy-Con and their lack of analog triggers.

Similarly *Nintendo Life* stated that accessing games comes at a "significant cost" and highlighted the system's 256GB storage among the cons of the console in their review, saying it will "fill up fast". *PC Gamer (US)* said not to buy the Switch 2 if you want cheap games, that the console has a "hefty price tag" and highlighted that the Switch 2 Joy-Con are still capable of getting stick drift.

# Original Nintendo Switch Owners Should Apply the Latest Firmware Update Now
The problem does not affect the Nintendo Switch 2.

#### Joe Hindy
Original Nintendo Switch owners have a security exploit to address. Nintendo released firmware version 23.0.0 on Sept. 9 and disclosed a vulnerability (PDF) the following day, recommending that all original Switch users update immediately. The Switch 2 isn’t affected by this particular issue, and Nintendo hasn’t shared specifics about what the exploit does. However, the company’s recommendation is clear, and the update that fixes these concerns is available now.

The vulnerability applies only to original Nintendo Switch owners who use the Send to Smartphone feature. This feature generates a QR code on the Switch that users can scan with a smartphone, allowing them to transfer game captures and screenshots directly to their phone.

The exploit also affects people playing Super Mario Kart: Home Circuit on the physical cartridge, as the game uses a QR code to establish a wireless link with nearby players.

## How to fix the problem
Nintendo released update 23.0.0 on Sept. 9, which fixes the exploit. It’s recorded as CVE-2026-82079, which is “a stock-based buffer overflow vulnerability” that lets attackers within wireless range execute code. It only affects the original Switch on firmware versions older than 23.0.0.

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered hits Nintendo Switch 2 Sept. 29, 2026, free for existing owners. Full launch analysis and Switch 2 port context.

Gaming

# Witcher 3 Remastered Hits Switch 2 Sept. 29 \[2026\]
Updated Sep 28, 2026 · 13 min read

CD PROJEKT RED’s remastered edition of *The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt* arrives on Nintendo Switch 2 tomorrow, September 29, 2026, closing an 11-year gap since Geralt of Rivia first stepped onto PC and PlayStation 4 in May 2015.

The release lands as part of a wider wave of AAA remasters and ports reaching Nintendo’s new hardware this year, and it arrives free for anyone who already owns the original game on the platforms CD PROJEKT RED has confirmed. This piece looks at what is actually confirmed for launch day, how the Switch 2 version fits into the console’s growing third-party library, and what the release signals about the remaster economy heading into 2027.

## What CD Projekt Red confirmed for September 29
The headline fact is simple: *The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered* ships on PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2 on September 29, 2026. CD PROJEKT RED’s announcement describes upgrades to visuals, gameplay, performance, and other unspecified features, without publishing a granular patch-note style breakdown ahead of launch.

Existing owners on GOG, Steam, Epic Games Store, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S get the remastered version as a free upgrade, no repurchase required. Switch owners of the original 2019 port also get a free claim path to the Switch 2 version once it releases.

That free-upgrade model is a deliberate contrast to how some publishers have handled remasters this generation, charging $10 to $40 for what amounts to a visual refresh. Our earlier coverage on CDPR’s decision to skip the upsell entirely goes deeper into the business logic behind that call.

The remastered base game folds in both expansions, *Hearts of Stone* and *Blood and Wine*, at no additional cost for existing owners. That bundling matters for the Switch 2 conversation specifically, because it means the portable version isn’t a stripped-down base-game-only release the way some past Switch ports trimmed content to hit performance targets.

## Why the Switch 2 version is the story, not the remaster itself
PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S owners already have a version of *The Witcher 3* that runs at or near 60 frames per second with ray tracing options. For them, the remaster is an incremental visual and technical bump on hardware that was already capable.

Switch 2 is the platform where the question actually matters: can Nintendo’s new hardware, which sits well below PS5 and Xbox Series X in raw compute, run an open-world RPG of this scale without the compromises that defined the original Switch 1 port back in 2019?

Switch 2’s silicon jump changes the baseline math entirely, and CD PROJEKT RED building the remaster natively for the new hardware, rather than porting the 2019 Switch 1 build forward, is the more relevant technical story for anyone deciding whether to play on the go.

No official resolution, frame rate, graphics-mode, or download-size numbers for the Switch 2 build had been published as of this writing. Any specific technical claim circulating ahead of launch should be treated as unconfirmed until CD PROJEKT RED or a hands-on outlet publishes tested figures once the update goes live.

## The Switch 2 port wave: Witcher 3 is not an outlier
*The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered* is landing in the middle of a genuinely crowded season for ambitious third-party ports chasing Switch 2’s new hardware ceiling.

*Diablo 4: Age of Hatred Collection* reached Switch 2 earlier this month, bundling two expansions into a $69.99 package, evidence that Nintendo’s new console can now carry live-service, loot-heavy ARPGs that would have been unthinkable on the original hardware.

At the more demanding end of that spectrum sits Rayman Legends Retold, whose PC requirements reportedly call for an RTX 4080-class GPU for 4K/60 performance while still being confirmed for a Switch 2 release.

That gap between PC recommended specs and a portable console target is exactly why hands-on impressions of games like the *Witcher 3* remaster matter so much this year: publishers are making increasingly bold bets that Switch 2’s architecture and its DLSS-style upscaling tools can close a hardware gap that would have been unbridgeable on Switch 1.

| Game | Switch 2 status | Notable detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered | Releases Sept. 29, 2026 | Free upgrade for existing owners; includes both expansions |
| Diablo 4: Age of Hatred Collection | Released Sept. 2026 | $69.99, bundles two expansions |
| Metal Gear Solid 4 Remaster | Released 2026 | Confirmed 60fps by Digital Foundry testing |
| Rayman Legends Retold | Confirmed for Switch 2 | PC specs reportedly target RTX 4080 for 4K/60 |
| Control Resonant | PC specs published | RTX 4070 Ti recommended for 60 FPS on PC |

## CD Projekt Red’s business calculus
A free, high-quality remaster functions as sustained marketing for that upcoming title. Every Switch 2 owner who claims the free Witcher 3 upgrade, plays through 100-plus hours of Geralt’s story, and comes away impressed is a warmer prospective buyer for Witcher 4 than one reached through a traditional ad campaign.

There’s a hardware-sales angle here too, one that benefits Nintendo more directly than CD PROJEKT RED. A widely known, well-reviewed RPG landing free for anyone who already owns it gives existing Switch and Switch 1 owners on the fence about upgrading a concrete reason to buy Switch 2 hardware now rather than waiting.

## Historical context: from 2015 launch to 2026 remaster
That earlier update was framed as a free upgrade for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S owners with targeted improvements; this year’s remaster spans four platforms simultaneously, including a from-the-ground-up Switch 2 build, and is being marketed with the “Remastered” label rather than as a next-gen patch.

It’s the first time CD PROJEKT RED has treated a Switch release of the game as a day-one platform alongside PC and the PlayStation/Xbox family rather than a delayed follow-up port, which is itself a signal of how much confidence the studio has in Switch 2’s hardware ceiling compared to its predecessor.

## Market impact: what a free AAA remaster does to a launch window
Switch 2 launched into a console market still working through a hardware supply crunch tied to broader memory chip shortages that have pushed up component costs across the industry this year. Against that backdrop, a free, marquee-name RPG landing on the platform functions as a low-cost way for Nintendo to add perceived value to hardware that’s already selling at a premium relative to its predecessor.

Open-world RPGs releasing in 2026 and 2027 are being built against a much higher visual and systemic bar, and keeping *The Witcher 3* in active rotation, especially on a growing platform like Switch 2, extends the commercial life of a decade-old title without requiring the studio to divert resources away from Witcher 4 development.

| Milestone | Date | Platform(s) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original launch | May 2015 | PC, PS4, Xbox One |
| Switch port | October 2019 | Nintendo Switch |
| Next-gen update | December 2022 | PS5, Xbox Series X\|S, PC |
| Remastered edition | September 29, 2026 | PC, PS5, Xbox Series X\|S, Switch 2 |

## What’s still unconfirmed heading into launch
It’s worth being precise about what CD PROJEKT RED has and hasn’t said publicly. The company has not published a standalone retail price for the Switch 2 version for buyers who don’t already own the base game on a qualifying platform. It has not released target resolution, frame rate, or graphics-mode details for the Switch 2 build, docked or handheld. No download size has been disclosed.

Expect the most reliable data points, docked and handheld resolution figures, sustained frame rate under load, and loading times, to surface within the first 24 to 48 hours after the September 29 release, largely from technical-analysis outlets running side-by-side comparisons against the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S versions.

## Predictions: what happens after launch day
- Expect the first wave of technical breakdowns within 48 hours of the September 29 release, likely including a Digital Foundry-style frame rate and resolution analysis comparing docked and handheld Switch 2 modes against PS5 and Xbox Series X\|S.

- The free-upgrade model will likely become the reference point other publishers get measured against the next time a studio tries to charge for a remaster of a game that’s over five years old.
- Switch 2’s third-party library credibility will keep building through Q4 2026 as more mid-generation remasters and ports target the platform, following the pattern set by Diablo 4, MGS4, and now Witcher 3.

- CD PROJEKT RED will likely use Witcher 3 Remastered’s Switch 2 reception, positive or negative, as a data point in its own public messaging about Witcher 4’s scope and platform ambitions.
- If performance reviews land well, expect a modest bump in Switch 2 hardware attach-rate commentary from Nintendo in its next quarterly investor update, framed around third-party AAA availability rather than first-party software alone.

## How to claim the free upgrade
For existing owners, the process is designed to require no manual repurchase. GOG, Steam, Epic Games Store, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S owners of the base game receive the Remastered version as an automatic free upgrade tied to their existing library entry. Switch owners of the original Wild Hunt release get a claim path for the free Switch 2 version once the update goes live on September 29.

Anyone without an existing copy can pre-purchase now through Battle.net or directly via the Nintendo Switch 2 storefront, though CD PROJEKT RED has not disclosed what that standalone purchase will cost.

Both included expansions, Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine, come bundled into the remastered base game for existing owners at no extra charge, meaning anyone who completed the story years ago and skipped the DLC now has a reason to go back in with a technically improved build across all four confirmed platforms.

## Frequently asked questions
**When does The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered release on Nintendo Switch 2?** September 29, 2026, alongside PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S versions.

**Is the Switch 2 version free if I already own The Witcher 3?** Yes, if you own the original game on Nintendo Switch, you can claim the Remastered Switch 2 version for free once it releases. Owners on GOG, Steam, Epic Games Store, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S also receive a free upgrade.

**Does the remaster include the expansions?** Yes. Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine are both included in the remastered base game, and existing owners get them at no additional cost.

**How much does the Switch 2 version cost for new buyers?** CD PROJEKT RED has not published a specific standalone price as of this writing. Pre-purchase is open through the Nintendo Switch 2 storefront and Battle.net.

**What resolution and frame rate will Switch 2 run at?** No official resolution or frame rate targets have been confirmed by CD PROJEKT RED ahead of launch. Independent technical testing is expected within days of the September 29 release.

**How is this different from the 2022 PS5/Xbox Series X update?** The 2022 update was a targeted next-gen patch adding ray tracing and performance improvements. The 2026 remaster spans four platforms including a native Switch 2 build and is branded as a full remaster rather than a next-gen patch.
